concept.name: Cancel-to-trade ratio
concept.definition: The ratio of cancelled orders (or cancelled quantity) to executed trades over a period - a standard metric of messaging intensity. The CFTC's Technology Advisory Committee working group listed cancel-to-fill ratios among the objective forms of measurement for the recurring high message rates characteristic of high-frequency trading.
concept.intuition: It counts how many quotes die for every trade that actually prints.
concept.mechanics: Computed per participant, instrument, or whole market over a session; exchanges and regulators monitor it to gauge system load, characterize quoting behavior, and detect potentially abusive messaging patterns.
concept.formula: CTR = N_cancelled orders / N_executed trades (or cancelled volume / traded volume) over a period.
concept.failure_modes: Appropriate levels vary enormously by asset class, venue, and strategy, so cross-market comparisons mislead; the ratio alone cannot distinguish benign market making from manipulative quote stuffing.
concept.misconceptions: A high cancel-to-trade ratio is not per se evidence of manipulation - passive electronic market making mechanically generates high cancel rates as quotes track a moving market.
concept.example: A firm cancels 40,000 orders and is filled on 800 in a session, a cancel-to-trade ratio of 50 to 1.

citations.source: CFTC, Concept Release on Risk Controls and System Safeguards for Automated Trading Environments, 78 FR 56542
citations.section: Part II.A.1, TAC working group HFT attributes (cancel-to-fill ratios)
